# Fremont by the Numbers — full text

> Fremont by the Numbers is a data aggregator built using Claude. It republishes figures that public sources have already published about Fremont, California, and shows each figure with its source and date. Data as of 2026-10-26. Links in this file marked "source" go to the page a figure was read from.


---

# Fremont by the Numbers  (index.html)

Fremont by the Numbers is a data aggregator built using Claude. It gathers public figures about Fremont, California (housing, schools, safety, jobs and more) and links every number to its source.

## Fremont at a glance
Click any number to open its source in a new tab.
- Residents: **233,974** — Jan 1, 2026 · CA Dept. of Finance E-1 [source](https://dof.ca.gov/forecasting/demographics/estimates-e1/)
- Typical home value: **$1,439,805** (-1.5% vs a year ago) — Sep 30, 2026 · Zillow Research [source](https://www.zillow.com/fremont-ca/home-values/)
- Median household income: **$181,506** — 2020–2024 · Census QuickFacts profile [source](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/fremontcitycalifornia/PST045225)
- Happiest city in America (WalletHub): **#1** — of 182 cities · Mar 10, 2026 [source](https://wallethub.com/edu/happiest-places-to-live/32619)
- Typical asking rent (Zillow index): **$3,388** — Sep 30, 2026 · Zillow Research [source](https://www.zillow.com/research/data/)
- Fremont Unified schools in California’s top 100 for their level (U.S. News): **9 of 37** — 3 high, 3 middle and 3 elementary schools · 2026–27 · U.S. News · 37 schools have a numbered state rank [source](https://www.usnews.com/education/best-high-schools/california/districts/fremont-unified-school-district-111898)

## Explore by topic
- [Rent & Housing](rent.html): $3,388 typical asking rent, Sep 2026 (Zillow)
- [Schools](schools.html): 93.1% Fremont Unified four-year graduation rate, class of 2025
- [Food](food.html): 451 restaurants, bars and food-service businesses (2022 Economic Census)
- [Parks & Events](parks.html): 42.8% of the city is parkland, all agencies
- [City Data](city.html): 233,974 residents, Jan 1, 2026 (CA Dept. of Finance)
- [Crime & Safety](safety.html): 436 violent crimes reported in 2024 (CA DOJ)
- [Health Care](health.html): 2.8% of residents under 65 are uninsured (ACS 2020–2024)
- [Jobs](jobs.html): 4.5% unemployment rate, Aug 2026 (BLS/EDD); median household income $181,506
- [Startups](startups.html): 25,000 Tesla employees in Fremont, the city’s largest employer (City financial report, FY2024)

## About this site
A data aggregator built by JeffreyAiFudenna using Claude to gather data and write the code
Fremont by the Numbers does not run its own surveys or measurements. It collects figures that public sources have already published (the City of Fremont, the U.S. Census Bureau, California state agencies, Zillow, Redfin, news reports and others) and puts them in one place.
Claude did the gathering. Claude, Anthropic’s AI model, read each source, recorded the figure with the page it came from and the date it was read, and wrote the code for this site. AI can misread a source, so every number links back to where it came from: click it to open the source in a new tab and check.
Read the full methodology and source list


---

# Rent & Housing  (rent.html)

Typical rent, home prices, housing stock, new homes, utility bills, internet and child care costs in Fremont, California, each with its source and date.

## Headline numbers
- Typical asking rent (Zillow ZORI): **$3,388** (+6.0% vs a year ago) — Sep 30, 2026 · Zillow Research [source](https://www.zillow.com/research/data/)
- Median gross rent, all renters (Census ACS): **$2,933** — 2020–2024 · Census QuickFacts profile [source](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/fremontcitycalifornia/PST045225)
- Typical home value (Zillow ZHVI): **$1,439,805** (-1.5% vs a year ago) — Sep 30, 2026 · Zillow Research [source](https://www.zillow.com/fremont-ca/home-values/)
- Median sale price (Redfin): **$1,370,347** — Sep 2026 · Redfin. -6.5% vs a year ago [source](https://www.redfin.com/city/6671/CA/Fremont/housing-market)
- Renters paying 30%+ of income on rent: **43.3%** — 2020–2024 · More resident facts. 12,894 of 29,747 renter households with a computed ratio [source](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25070?g=160XX00US0626000)
Note: Zillow figures are modeled indexes of the middle tier of homes and rentals; Census figures are survey medians across everyone who already lives here, so they run lower than asking rents.

## Rent by bedroom
What Fremont renters pay, and what HUD considers a fair-market rent for the Oakland–Fremont area.

### Monthly rent by bedroom count
Census median gross rent (2020–2024) vs HUD Fair Market Rent (FY 2026)
| Item | Census median, 2020–2024 | HUD fair market rent, FY 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Studio | $2,306 | $2,142 |
| 1 bedroom | $2,455 | $2,385 |
| 2 bedrooms | $2,950 | $2,912 |
| 3 bedrooms | $3,501 | $3,724 |
| 4 bedrooms | $3,501 | $4,413 |
Source note: Census ACS table B25031 (Fremont city) and HUD FY 2026 Fair Market Rents, Oakland–Fremont HUD Metro FMR Area. Census medians for 3- and 4-bedroom homes are capped at $3,501 (“top-coded”), so the true figures are higher.View source: Census ACS 2020–2024, table B25031 View source: HUD: FY 2026 Fair Market Rents

### Median rent in two Census survey periods
Census median gross rent, 2015–2019 vs 2020–2024 (not adjusted to a common year’s dollars)
| Item | 2015–2019 | 2020–2024 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Studio | $1,830 | $2,306 |
| 1 bedroom | $2,013 | $2,455 |
| 2 bedrooms | $2,392 | $2,950 |
| 3 bedrooms | $2,792 | $3,501 |
| 4 bedrooms | $3,127 | $3,501 |
Source note: Census ACS table B25031, 5-year estimates. Each period is stated in its own final year’s dollars, so the gap mixes rent growth with inflation.View source: Census ACS 2020–2024, table B25031

## Housing stock
- Housing units: **81,579** — 2020–2024 · More resident facts [source](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDP5Y2024.DP04?g=160XX00US0626000)
- Homes that are owner-occupied: **60.8%** — 2020–2024 · Census QuickFacts profile [source](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/fremontcitycalifornia/PST045225)
- Median year homes were built: **1979** — 2020–2024 · More resident facts [source](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25035?g=160XX00US0626000)
- Rental vacancy rate: **4.8%** — 2020–2024 · More resident facts [source](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDP5Y2024.DP04?g=160XX00US0626000)
- Median monthly owner costs, with a mortgage: **$4,000+** — 2020–2024 · Census QuickFacts profile [source](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/fremontcitycalifornia/PST045225)
- Regulated affordable rental homes: **3,656** — Updated Oct 17, 2025 · City of Fremont [source](https://www.fremont.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/449/638977635550300000)
Note: Census figures are 2020–2024 five-year survey estimates for the city of Fremont. The owner-cost figure is capped at $4,000 in the survey, so the real median is higher.

## Building more homes
Fremont’s state housing target for 2023–2031 and how far along it is.
- Homes permitted in 2025: **549** — Calendar 2025 · City of Fremont 2025 Annual Progress Report staff report [source](https://fremontcityca.iqm2.com/Citizens/Detail_LegiFile.aspx?CssClass=&Frame=&ID=5659&MediaPosition=&MeetingID=2073&amp=&amp=&amp=&amp=)
- Of which backyard units (ADUs): **177** — Calendar 2025 · City of Fremont 2025 Annual Progress Report staff report [source](https://fremontcityca.iqm2.com/Citizens/Detail_LegiFile.aspx?CssClass=&Frame=&ID=5659&MediaPosition=&MeetingID=2073&amp=&amp=&amp=&amp=)
- State target for 2023–2031 (RHNA): **12,897** — 2023–2031 · City of Fremont Housing Element page and 2025 APR staff report [source](https://fremont.gov/government/departments/community-development/planning-building-permit-services/plans-maps-guidelines/general-plan/housing-element)
- Still to permit after 2025: **11,407** — After 2025 · City of Fremont 2025 Annual Progress Report staff report [source](https://fremontcityca.iqm2.com/Citizens/Detail_LegiFile.aspx?CssClass=&Frame=&ID=5659&MediaPosition=&MeetingID=2073&amp=&amp=&amp=&amp=)
- Affordable homes about to start construction: **918** — Fall 2026 · Hoodline [source](https://hoodline.com/2026/10/fremont-project-set-to-break-ground-on-335-unit-downtown-development-first-of-918-affordable-homes/)

## Utilities and taxes
The regular bills on top of rent or a mortgage.
- Average monthly electric bill, Ava Bright Choice (338 kWh): **$138.33** — Rates as of Mar 2026 · Ava Community Energy / PG&E 2026 joint rate comparison. Fremont’s default plan, Renewable 100, costs about 1.75 cents per kWh more. [source](https://avaenergy.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Joint-Rate-Mailer-2025-Power-Mix-2025-Vintage-260616_Eng.pdf)
- Average monthly gas bill (31 therms, PG&E territory): **$86.54** — Effective Mar 1, 2026 · PG&E, Gas Rate Advisory (March 2026) [source](https://www.pge.com/assets/pge/docs/account/rate-plans/gas-rate-advisory-0326.pdf)
- Typical home water bill, every two months: **$155.03** — From Mar 1, 2026 · Alameda County Water District [source](https://acwd.org/115/Water-Rates)
- Sewer charge per home, per year: **$661.15** — FY 2026–27 · Union Sanitary District Ordinance 31.41 [source](https://unionsanitary.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Ordinance-No.-31.41.pdf)
- Garbage, 32-gallon cart, per month: **$48.84** — 2026–27 · Republic Services, Fremont rates [source](https://www.republicservices.com/sites/default/files/legacy_documents/Muni/California/Fremont/Fremont-City-Rates-2026-2027.pdf)
- Sales tax rate: **10.25%** — From Oct 1, 2026 · CDTFA tax rates [source](https://cdtfa.ca.gov/taxes-and-fees/rates.aspx)
- Property tax base rate (plus voter-approved bonds): **1%** — FY 2025–26 · Alameda County Auditor [source](https://www.acgov.org/board/bos_calendar/documents/DocsAgendaReg_09_09_25/GENERAL%20ADMINISTRATION/Regular%20Calendar/Auditor_391480.pdf)

### Natural gas and the Ava discount

Note: Electricity is sold by Ava Community Energy (the East Bay’s public power agency) and delivered by PG&E. Water comes from Alameda County Water District; sewer service from Union Sanitary District; garbage from Republic Services under the city contract.

- More resident facts: ACS 2020–2024 measures (age, households, income, housing stock, cost burden, veterans, disability) and County Business Patterns 2023 jobs. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Rent by bedroom: Census ACS median gross rent by bedrooms (2015–2019 and 2020–2024; capped at $3,500) and HUD Fair Market Rents FY2025–26 for the Oakland-Fremont area. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Zillow history: Monthly Zillow Home Value Index and Observed Rent Index for Fremont city, Jan 2015 to Sep 2026, from Zillow Research city-level files. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Voters and city facts: Nov 2024 turnout (Alameda County ROV), May 2026 registration by party (CA Secretary of State), affordable units, city FTEs and credit rating (City of Fremont). Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Housing permits and target: Units permitted in 2025 and progress toward Fremont's 2023–2031 RHNA target, from the city's 2025 Annual Progress Report staff report (Planning Commission, Feb 26, 2026). Self-reported by the city; HCD does not verify it.
- Housing target by income: RHNA target, units permitted 2023–2025, units remaining, and 2025 permits by income level, from the city's 2025 Annual Progress Report staff report. ADUs are assigned to income levels using ABAG affordability assumptions.
- Child care and utilities: Alameda County child care costs (2022) and licensed spaces (2023) from kidsdata.org; electricity rate and bill (Ava/PG&E, Mar 2026); ACWD water use per person (FY 2023–24). Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Gas and internet: PG&E residential gas rate and average bill, Ava vs PG&E rate difference, internet providers, coverage and advertised prices for Fremont. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Costs, transit and services: Utility bills, tax rates, transit ridership, hospitals, voters, energy and hazards, each from the agency named in its row. Read Oct 24, 2026.

# Schools  (schools.html)

Fremont Unified graduation rates, test results, high school rankings and a finder for every elementary, middle and high school, each with its source and date.

## Fremont Unified at a glance
- Students enrolled: **32,883** — 2025–26 · CDE District Profile and Ed-Data [source](https://www.cde.ca.gov/sdprofile/details.aspx?cds=01611760000000)
- K–12 schools: **41** — 2025–26 · FUSD About page [source](https://fremontunified.org/about/)
- Four-year graduation rate: **93.1%** — Class of 2025 (2024–25) · CDE adjusted cohort graduation rate. California: 87.5% [source](https://fremontunified.org/news/2025-dash/)
- Proficient or advanced in English: **71.7%** — 2025–26 · CAASPP Smarter Balanced results. California: 49.3% [source](https://caaspp-elpac.ets.org/caaspp/DashViewReportSB?ps=true&lstTestYear=2026&lstTestType=B&lstGroup=1&lstSubGroup=1&lstSchoolType=A&lstGrade=13&lstCounty=01&lstDistrict=61176-000&lstSchool=0000000)
- Proficient or advanced in math: **67.9%** — 2025–26 · CAASPP Smarter Balanced results. California: 38.4% [source](https://caaspp-elpac.ets.org/caaspp/DashViewReportSB?ps=true&lstTestYear=2026&lstTestType=B&lstGroup=1&lstSubGroup=1&lstSchoolType=A&lstGrade=13&lstCounty=01&lstDistrict=61176-000&lstSchool=0000000)
- Students per teacher: **21.4** — 2025–26 · CDE staffing data, via Ed-Data. California: 20.4 [source](https://www.ed-data.org/district/Alameda/Fremont-Unified)
Note: Fremont Unified serves nearly all of the city. Test figures are the share of students meeting the state standard on the 2025–26 Smarter Balanced tests in grades 3–8 and 11.

# Food  (food.html)

Grocery budgets, food price inflation, restaurants and grocery stores in Fremont, California, each with its source and date.

## What food costs
- Living-wage food budget, two adults and two kids, per month: **$1,240** — 2026 · MIT Living Wage Calculator, Alameda County (annual figure ÷ 12) [source](https://livingwage.mit.edu/counties/06001)
- Living-wage food budget, one adult, per month: **$424** — 2026 · MIT Living Wage Calculator, Alameda County (annual figure ÷ 12) [source](https://livingwage.mit.edu/counties/06001)
Note: No agency publishes Fremont-only food prices. The budgets above are Alameda County living-wage estimates from MIT, and the price changes below cover the San Francisco–Oakland–Hayward area, which includes Fremont.

## How fast food prices are rising
Consumer Price Index for the San Francisco–Oakland–Hayward area, which includes Fremont.
- Grocery prices, change over the past year: **2.2%** — Aug 2025–Aug 2026 · BLS, Consumer Price Index, San Francisco-Oakland-Hayward – August 2026 (released Sep 11, 2026) [source](https://www.bls.gov/regions/west/news-release/consumerpriceindex_sanfrancisco.htm)
- Restaurant prices, change over the past year: **4.1%** — Aug 2025–Aug 2026 · BLS, Consumer Price Index, San Francisco-Oakland-Hayward – August 2026 [source](https://www.bls.gov/regions/west/news-release/consumerpriceindex_sanfrancisco.htm)
- All food, change over the past year: **3.1%** — Aug 2025–Aug 2026 · BLS, Consumer Price Index, San Francisco-Oakland-Hayward – August 2026 [source](https://www.bls.gov/regions/west/news-release/consumerpriceindex_sanfrancisco.htm)

# Parks & Events  (parks.html)

Parks, trails, annual events, community facilities and weather in Fremont, California, each with its source and date.

## Parks at a glance
- City parks: **64** — Feb 2022 · City of Fremont Parks & Recreation Master Plan [source](https://fremont.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/9619/638611250926530000)
- Acres of city parkland: **1,224** — Feb 2022 · City of Fremont Parks & Recreation Master Plan [source](https://fremont.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/9619/638611250926530000)
- Acres of parkland, all agencies: **17,739** — 2026 · Trust for Public Land ParkServe. Includes regional parks and the Don Edwards wildlife refuge. [source](https://parkserve.tpl.org/downloads/pdfs/Fremont_CA.pdf)
- Share of the city that is parkland: **42.8%** — 2026 · Trust for Public Land ParkServe. National median for big cities: 15%. [source](https://parkserve.tpl.org/downloads/pdfs/Fremont_CA.pdf)
- Residents within a 10-minute walk of a park: **70.4%** — 2026 · Trust for Public Land ParkServe [source](https://parkserve.tpl.org/downloads/pdfs/Fremont_CA.pdf)
- ParkScore rank among the 100 largest U.S. cities: **#43** — 2026 · Trust for Public Land [source](https://www.tpl.org/parkscore)

## Trails, courts and programs
- Miles of trails in Fremont’s network (City figure): **61** — 2026 · City of Fremont. The city’s 30-year goal is 140 miles. [source](https://www.fremont.gov/government/departments/parks-planning-design/park-planning)
- Miles of city-owned multi-use trails: **23** — Feb 2022 · City of Fremont [source](https://fremont.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/9619/638611250926530000)
- Dedicated pickleball courts at Central Park Knoll: **8** — Opened Jun 2024 · City of Fremont [source](https://www.fremont.gov/government/departments/parks-planning-design/design-projects/central-park-knoll-pickleball-court-lighting)
- Off-leash dog parks: **2** — 2026 · Macaroni KID Fremont [source](https://fremont.macaronikid.com/guides/606e76bdc5999c19f4cb4671/dog-parks-in-fremont-newark-and-union-city)
- Recreation program registrants in a year: **20,000** — FY 2019/20 · City of Fremont. Last published figure, pre-pandemic (FY 2019–20). [source](https://fremont.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/1089/637806234781330000)
- Aqua Adventure water park, non-resident admission: **$27** — 2026 season · 510 Families [source](https://www.510families.com/aqua-adventure-waterpark)

## City government and budget
- Operating budget, all funds: **$427M** — FY 2026–27, as proposed · Hoodline [source](https://hoodline.com/2026/07/fremont-council-slams-brakes-on-half-cent-tax-hike-before-november-vote-6944803/)
- General fund spending: **$289M** — FY 2026–27, proposed · Citizen Portal report of the proposed budget [source](https://citizenportal.ai/articles/8258598/California/Alameda-County/Fremont/Fremont-proposes-2891-million-operating-budget-for-202627-council-asks-for-deferredmaintenance-list)
- City employees (full-time equivalent): **1,006.6** — FY 2025–26 proposed budget · City of Fremont FY 2025/26 Proposed Budget [source](https://www.fremont.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/18117/638828954844570000)
- S&P bond rating: **AA+ (stable)** — As reported in the FY 2024-25 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report · City of Fremont FY 2024-25 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report [source](https://www.fremont.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/19533)
Note: Budget figures are from the City’s proposed FY 2026–27 budget, as reported by Hoodline and Citizen Portal in May and July 2026. The council adopted a budget on June 9, 2026, but the adopted document was not found online, so adopted totals may differ. The employee count is from the FY 2025/26 proposed budget and the bond rating from the City’s FY 2024-25 financial report (AA+, stable); it was not checked against S&P directly.

- Asian communities: Share of Fremont residents by Asian group (alone), ACS 2020–2024 table DP05. Read Oct 24, 2026.

- Top FremontApp requests: Ten most common FremontApp request types, Jul 1–Sep 30, 2026, from the city's FremontApp dashboard.
- Point-in-time counts: Unhoused residents in Fremont from point-in-time counts, 2017–2026, as shown on the city's Homeless Response dashboard.
- Homeless response by month: Monthly cleanups, encampments fully cleared, outreach visits and FremontApp homeless-related reports, Jul 2025–Sep 2026, from the city's Homeless Response dashboard. The dashboard's headline app-report count (715) exceeds the sum of these rows (687).
- Climate indicators: EVs registered, trees planted and pounds of food recovered in 2025, from the city's Climate Action dashboard.

- Emissions by sector: Community greenhouse gas emissions (metric tons CO2e) by sector for inventory years 2005, 2010, 2015 and 2018, and the city's 2030 goal, read from the chart data on the city's Climate Action dashboard.

- EV charger permits: Electric vehicle charger permits issued in Fremont per year, 2021–2026 (2026 year to date), from the city's Climate Action dashboard.

- BART weekday exits: Average weekday exits at Fremont and Warm Springs stations, FY 2019, 2024 and 2025, averaged from BART daily station exits (DataSF). Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Highway traffic volumes: Caltrans 2024 annual average daily traffic at selected count points on highways through Fremont. Read Oct 24, 2026.

Crime, police, fire department and traffic safety figures for Fremont, California, each with its source and date.

## Crime in 2024, the last complete year
- Violent crimes reported: **436** — 2024 · CA DOJ OpenJustice. -8.2% vs 2023 [source](https://openjustice.doj.ca.gov/data)
- Violent crimes per 1,000 residents: **1.9** — 2024 · CA DOJ crimes ÷ Dept. of Finance population, Jan 1, 2025 [source](https://openjustice.doj.ca.gov/data)
- Property crimes reported: **5,233** — 2024 · CA DOJ OpenJustice. -17.1% vs 2023 [source](https://openjustice.doj.ca.gov/data)
- Property crimes per 1,000 residents: **22.4** — 2024 · CA DOJ crimes ÷ Dept. of Finance population, Jan 1, 2025 [source](https://openjustice.doj.ca.gov/data)
- Safest Cities rank (WalletHub): **#14** — of 182 cities · Oct 19, 2026 [source](https://wallethub.com/edu/safest-cities-in-america/41926)
- Residents who feel safe in Fremont: **70%** — Dec 2025 (n=636, ±4.0%) · City of Fremont 2025 Community Survey [source](https://www.fremont.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/19926/639087261651070000)

This page uses the state Department of Justice file. Rates per 1,000 residents divide 2024 crimes by the Department of Finance population for Jan 1, 2025 (233,428).

## The hospitals
Washington Hospital is run by a public health-care district; Kaiser Permanente Fremont Medical Center serves Kaiser members. Fremont Hospital is a private psychiatric hospital.

# Jobs  (jobs.html)

Unemployment, income, largest employers, wages, industries and commuting in Fremont, California, each with its source and date.

## Headline numbers
- Fremont unemployment rate: **4.5%** — Aug 2026 · BLS/EDD Local Area Unemployment Statistics. A year earlier: 4.9%. Not seasonally adjusted. [source](https://ycharts.com/indicators/fremont_ca_unemployment_rate)
- Median household income: **$181,506** — 2020–2024 · Census QuickFacts profile [source](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/fremontcitycalifornia/PST045225)
- Income per person: **$77,049** — 2020–2024 · Census QuickFacts profile [source](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/fremontcitycalifornia/PST045225)
- Fremont minimum wage, per hour: **$18.05** — Effective Jul 1, 2026 · City of Fremont news release 'Fremont Minimum Wage Increase to $18.05 on July 1. California: $16.90. Rises each July 1 with inflation. [source](https://www.fremont.gov/Home/Components/News/News/1724/1067)
- Adults in the labor force: **67.9%** — 2020–2024 · Census QuickFacts profile [source](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/fremontcitycalifornia/PST045225)
- Households earning $200,000 or more: **44.8%** — 2020–2024 · More resident facts [source](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19001?g=160XX00US0626000)

## Jobs in Fremont vs jobs held by residents
In the City’s Housing Element, Fremont had about 5% more jobs than employed residents, so on balance it draws in more workers than it sends out.
- Jobs located in Fremont (Housing Element): **93,659** — c. 2018 · City of Fremont [source](https://fremont.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/12773/638151808164530000)
- Employed Fremont residents (same table and year): **89,027** — c. 2018 · City of Fremont [source](https://fremont.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/12773/638151808164530000)
- Jobs per employed resident (Housing Element): **1.05** — c. 2018 · City of Fremont. Above 1.0 means a net importer of workers. [source](https://fremont.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/12773/638151808164530000)
- Employed Fremont residents, 2024 (ACS): **118,511** — 2024 (ACS) · Data USA. A newer survey count. Do not compare it with the c. 2018 jobs figure. [source](https://datausa.io/profile/geo/fremont-ca)
- Private-sector jobs in Fremont ZIP codes (Census): **125,388** — Mar 2023 · More resident facts [source](https://data.census.gov/table/CBP2023.CB2300CBP?g=860XX00US94536,94538,94539,94555)
- Fremont jobs related to manufacturing (City of Fremont): **35%** — Undated · City of Fremont Economic Development [source](https://www.fremont.gov/government/departments/economic-development/local-economy-overview/city-profile)
- Workers covered by layoff (WARN) notices in 2025: **513** — 2025 · LaborCurrent [source](https://laborcurrent.com/layoffs/california/fremont)
Note: The first three cards come from one table in the City’s 2023–2031 Housing Element, which draws on Census LEHD data from about 2018 (jobs come from administrative records, employed residents from survey data). The 2024 residents count (Census ACS) and the 2023 ZIP-code job count (Census County Business Patterns, which covers a wider area than the city limits) use different methods and are not meant to be compared with them.

- How Fremont gets to work: Census ACS 2020–2024 table DP03: workers 16+ by way of getting to work. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Shopping and dining: Restaurant and retail counts, jobs, taxable sales and major centers, from Census County Business Patterns, CDTFA and the City of Fremont. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Commercial vacancy: Office, R&D and industrial vacancy for the Fremont submarkets, Kidder Mathews 3Q 2026 reports. Read Oct 24, 2026.

# About, Sources & Methodology  (sources.html)

How Fremont by the Numbers works: a data aggregator built using Claude, its methodology, limitations, datasets and every source page.

## A data aggregator built using Claude
Fremont by the Numbers is a data aggregator. It does not run its own surveys, counts or measurements. It gathers figures that public sources have already published, such as the City of Fremont’s reports and dashboards, the U.S. Census Bureau, California state agencies, Zillow, Redfin and news coverage, and shows them in one place for people who live in, or are thinking about moving to, Fremont, California. Every number carries its source and the date it was read.

## Built by JeffreyAiFudenna
Fremont by the Numbers was built by JeffreyAiFudenna, using Claude to gather the data and write the code.

## The dataset was created using Claude
The research and data collection behind this site were done with Claude, Anthropic’s AI model, working from public sources. Claude read each source, recorded the figure together with the page it came from and the date it was read, flagged caveats such as incomplete years or county-level data, and wrote the code for this site. The site owner reviews the dataset before publishing. Because an AI can misread a source, the site is built so that you can check any number yourself.

## Click a number to see where it came from
Click or tap any stat card, table row or chart bar to open its source in a new tab (on a chart, tap the “View source” link under it). Where a figure comes from a report, the link opens the report or the publisher’s page for it. A few figures are simple arithmetic on published numbers (rates per 1,000 residents, shares, year-over-year changes); those link to the source of the underlying figures. If a link has moved, the Sources list below names the publisher so you can find the current page.

## What a number on this site means
- Every figure carries its period and source. “2020–2024” means a Census five-year survey estimate; a month or date means a count or index for that time.
- Fremont first. Figures are for the city of Fremont wherever they exist. When they do not, the page says so and uses Fremont’s ZIP codes, Alameda County, the Oakland–Fremont metro area or the Bay Area, in that order.
- Official before modeled, modeled before crowdsourced. Government counts and company statements come first; modeled indexes like Zillow’s are labeled; crowdsourced figures are used only where nothing else exists and are marked.
- Nothing is estimated here. Where a figure could not be found, the page leaves it out rather than guessing. A few derived figures (rates per 1,000 residents, shares, year-over-year changes) are simple arithmetic on the published numbers and say which population they use.
- Incomplete data is marked. Hollow points and bars in charts, and the “Incomplete” or “Year to date” labels, mean the period is not finished or the source has not finished reporting it.

## Known limitations
- The City of Fremont’s dashboards (fire incidents, homeless response, FremontApp, climate) publish no download, so those figures were read from the dashboards by hand.
- This site is compiled by an AI model from other organizations’ publications. It can make mistakes, and it cannot always reach a primary source; where it relied on a secondary source (a republisher, a news report or an encyclopedia transcription), the row says so. Please use the source links to confirm anything you plan to rely on.
- Fremont Police Department’s switch to incident-based (NIBRS) reporting in 2022 changes how crimes are counted, and the state’s 2025 crime file is incomplete for Fremont.
- Some figures exist only at the county or metro level (child care costs, gas bills, food price inflation, living-wage food budgets).
- Rankings such as WalletHub’s and U.S. News’s use their publishers’ own methods and weightings.

## Privacy
This site has no accounts, forms, ads or tracking cookies, and it does not collect personal information. The only thing it stores on your device is your light or dark mode choice. The site is hosted on Vercel, which keeps standard server logs and may count visits.

## Updates
On Oct 25, 2026 the site was trimmed: figures that were out of date, duplicated on another page, or not about Fremont itself (county, Bay Area, national or worldwide) were removed, so each fact now appears once. Each figure is refreshed when its source publishes a new release; the release calendar on the home page lists what is due next. The date in the header is the date the dataset was last checked. Corrections are welcome.

## Datasets behind the site
Each dataset is one file; its description says what it holds and when it was read.
- Adult health (CDC PLACES): Modeled adult health prevalence for Fremont with 95% ranges, CDC PLACES 2025 release (mostly 2023 data). Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Asian communities: Share of Fremont residents by Asian group (alone), ACS 2020–2024 table DP05. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- BART weekday exits: Average weekday exits at Fremont and Warm Springs stations, FY 2019, 2024 and 2025, averaged from BART daily station exits (DataSF). Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Census counts and estimate: Decennial Census counts for Fremont 1960–2020 (1960–2000 as compiled by MTC in 2021) and the Census Bureau's Vintage 2025 estimate for Jul 1, 2025 from QuickFacts. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Census QuickFacts profile: Fremont city profile from Census QuickFacts: mostly ACS 2020–2024 5-year survey estimates, with age and race from Census population estimates. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Child care and utilities: Alameda County child care costs (2022) and licensed spaces (2023) from kidsdata.org; electricity rate and bill (Ava/PG&E, Mar 2026); ACWD water use per person (FY 2023–24). Read Oct 24, 2026.
- City parks list: City of Fremont parks by name, type, status and acreage, from the city's park inventory. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- City rankings: Fremont's rank in 2025–26 national city rankings, read from each WalletHub ranking table (and Trust for Public Land ParkScore) on Oct 24, 2026, with category ranks and publication dates.
- City services and budget: FY 2026–27 budget (proposed general fund $289.1M plus about $138M other funds, about $427M in all; adopted Jun 9, 2026), police calls for service, and Fremont Unified enrollment. From news reports and agency pages, read Oct 24, 2026.
- Climate indicators: EVs registered, trees planted and pounds of food recovered in 2025, from the city's Climate Action dashboard.
- Commercial vacancy: Office, R&D and industrial vacancy for the Fremont submarkets, Kidder Mathews 3Q 2026 reports. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Costs, transit and services: Utility bills, tax rates, transit ridership, hospitals, voters, energy and hazards, each from the agency named in its row. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Crime clearances: Violent and property crimes reported and cleared: Fremont 2015–2025 and California 2020–2025. California DOJ Crimes and Clearances (July 2026 release). Read Oct 24, 2026.
- District trends: Fremont Unified by school year with state comparisons: enrollment, graduation, UC/CSU readiness, dropout, chronic absence, suspension, spending, teacher salary, staffing. CDE data via Ed-Data. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- DOF population estimates: California Department of Finance E-1 estimates for Fremont, Jan 1 2025 (revised) and Jan 1 2026 (provisional). Checked Oct 24, 2026 against DOF's own E-1 2026 press release (May 1, 2026).
- Emissions by sector: Community greenhouse gas emissions (metric tons CO2e) by sector for inventory years 2005, 2010, 2015 and 2018, and the city's 2030 goal, read from the chart data on the city's Climate Action dashboard.
- EV charger permits: Electric vehicle charger permits issued in Fremont per year, 2021–2026 (2026 year to date), from the city's Climate Action dashboard.
- Events and recreation: Signature annual events, Mission Peak, the 2022 Parks & Recreation Master Plan inventory, pickleball, dog parks, Aqua Adventure, recreation registrants and facilities. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Fatal crashes by year: Fatal crashes on Fremont city streets, 2014–2025, plus crashes the city lists separately as others. City of Fremont Safety Data and Trends. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Fire department summary: Full-year 2025 incident total from the city's incident-summaries page, plus stations and area covered from the city's Fremont Fire dashboard (refreshed Oct 23, 2026).
- Fire incidents by type, 2025: Fremont Fire Department incidents in 2025 by type (19,003 in all), from the incident-summaries page on fremont.gov. Replaces an earlier top-five table from the Power BI dashboard whose date range could not be confirmed. Read Oct 25, 2026.
- Fire incidents by year: Fremont Fire Department incidents per year, 2021–2025, read from the city's Power BI dashboard (refreshed Oct 23, 2026). The 2026 figure is left out because its date range could not be confirmed.
- Food costs: Grocery and restaurant price inflation (Bay Area CPI), MIT living-wage food costs for Alameda County, Fremont grocery and restaurant counts (2022 Economic Census), farmers' markets, CalFresh. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Food price inflation: Bay Area (SF–Oakland–Hayward) CPI for groceries, restaurants, all food and all items, each August 2018–2026, from BLS news releases. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Fremont Unified schools: Fremont Unified counts, enrollment, CAASPP 2025–26 results, four-year graduation rate (class of 2025) and staffing, from CDE (via Ed-Data), CAASPP and FUSD. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- FremontApp requests summary: Service requests created, closed and open and average days to close for Jul 1–Sep 30, 2026 (the dashboard's default range), from the city's FremontApp dashboard.
- Gas and internet: PG&E residential gas rate and average bill, Ava vs PG&E rate difference, internet providers, coverage and advertised prices for Fremont. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Hate crimes, Fremont: Hate crime incidents by year closed, Fremont PD, 2015–2025. California DOJ Hate Crimes file. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- High school rankings: Fremont Unified's five comprehensive high schools: U.S. News Best High Schools 2026–27 ranks and stats (prior-year ranks from FUSD's Aug 2025 release), plus CAASPP 2025–26 grade 11 results with district and state benchmarks. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Highway traffic volumes: Caltrans 2024 annual average daily traffic at selected count points on highways through Fremont. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Homeless response by month: Monthly cleanups, encampments fully cleared, outreach visits and FremontApp homeless-related reports, Jul 2025–Sep 2026, from the city's Homeless Response dashboard. The dashboard's headline app-report count (715) exceeds the sum of these rows (687).
- Hospitals, coverage and providers: CMS Care Compare stars, Leapfrog safety grades, ER times and volumes for Washington Hospital and Kaiser Fremont; clinics; insurance coverage by type (ACS 2024) and Medi-Cal. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Housing permits and target: Units permitted in 2025 and progress toward Fremont's 2023–2031 RHNA target, from the city's 2025 Annual Progress Report staff report (Planning Commission, Feb 26, 2026). Self-reported by the city; HCD does not verify it.
- Housing target by income: RHNA target, units permitted 2023–2025, units remaining, and 2025 permits by income level, from the city's 2025 Annual Progress Report staff report. ADUs are assigned to income levels using ABAG affordability assumptions.
- How Fremont gets to work: Census ACS 2020–2024 table DP03: workers 16+ by way of getting to work. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Languages at home: Language spoken at home, residents 5 and older, ACS 2020–2024 table C16001. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Largest employers: Fremont's ten largest employers from the City's FY2024 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report principal-employers table, as transcribed on Wikipedia; the FY2025 ACFR (Dec 2025) should be used to refresh. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Largest funding rounds: Largest recent funding rounds and IPOs by Fremont-linked companies, 2022–2026 (some have contested or dual headquarters, noted in each row), each row citing its own source; not an exhaustive total. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Leapfrog safety grades: Leapfrog Hospital Safety Grades for Washington Hospital and Kaiser Fremont, Spring 2023 to Spring 2026. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- More resident facts: ACS 2020–2024 measures (age, households, income, housing stock, cost burden, veterans, disability) and County Business Patterns 2023 jobs. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- OTS crash rankings: California Office of Traffic Safety 2023 crash rankings for Fremont among 62 cities of 100,001–250,000 people (1 = worst). Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Parks and facilities: City park counts and acreage, Trust for Public Land ParkScore, libraries and community centers. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Pavement condition: MTC Pavement Condition Index (three-year moving average) 2022–2024 for Fremont and the Bay Area, Jan 2026 update. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Point-in-time counts: Unhoused residents in Fremont from point-in-time counts, 2017–2026, as shown on the city's Homeless Response dashboard.
- Police and survey facts: Fremont PD calls for service, staffing and 911 answer times, plus the City's 2025 Community Survey safety results. Each row names its source. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Police staffing: Funded sworn and civilian positions for Fremont, 2015–2025. California DOJ Law Enforcement Personnel file. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Redfin market snapshot: Redfin housing market pages for Fremont city (Sep 2026) and ZIP codes 94536, 94538, 94539 and 94555 (Aug 2026), read Oct 24, 2026. Redfin's terms for republishing these figures are not yet confirmed.
- Regional parks in Fremont: East Bay Regional Park District parks in Fremont with acreage, from EBRPD park pages and news releases. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Rent by bedroom: Census ACS median gross rent by bedrooms (2015–2019 and 2020–2024; capped at $3,500) and HUD Fair Market Rents FY2025–26 for the Oakland-Fremont area. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Reported crime by city: Violent and property crimes by type and year, 2015–2025, for Fremont. California DOJ OpenJustice, Crimes and Clearances file (published July 2026). 2025 is incomplete for Fremont.
- Residents' industries: Employed residents 16+ by industry, top seven, ACS 2020–2024 table C24050. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- School finder data: Every Fremont Unified elementary, middle and high school: CAASPP 2025–26 and 2024–25 results, DataQuest 2025–26 enrollment, Ed-Data 2024–25 chronic absence and suspension, 2025–26 low-income share, and U.S. News ranks. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Shopping and dining: Restaurant and retail counts, jobs, taxable sales and major centers, from Census County Business Patterns, CDTFA and the City of Fremont. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Source pages: Every page used for a figure on this dashboard, with publisher and what it supports. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Startup ecosystem: Company counts from Crunchbase and VCBacked.co (crowdsourced directories), unicorns and IPOs, the City of Fremont's own claims on tech and manufacturing firms, patent holders, Warm Springs Innovation District and rankings. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Stores by type: Retail establishments in Fremont by category (437 stores in all), 2022 Economic Census, retail trade, Fremont city. The total matches the 2022 Economic Census retail store count. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Streets and traffic facts: Street network facts from the City of Fremont, Fremont PD and MTC, fatal-crash victim shares, and the 2025 Community Survey traffic results. Each row names its source. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Top FremontApp requests: Ten most common FremontApp request types, Jul 1–Sep 30, 2026, from the city's FremontApp dashboard.
- Unemployment, wages and jobs: Fremont city unemployment rate (BLS/EDD LAUS via YCharts), jobs located in Fremont vs employed residents (Housing Element/LEHD), city minimum wage, median earnings (ACS 2024), WARN layoffs, commute shares. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Vehicles by fuel and ZIP: Light-duty registrations by fuel type for Fremont ZIPs 94536, 94538, 94539, 94555, as of Jan 1, 2020 and Dec 31, 2025. California DMV via data.ca.gov. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Voters and city facts: Nov 2024 turnout (Alameda County ROV), May 2026 registration by party (CA Secretary of State), affordable units, city FTEs and credit rating (City of Fremont). Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Weather by month: NOAA 1991–2020 climate normals for the Fremont station: average high, low and rainfall by month. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Zillow history: Monthly Zillow Home Value Index and Observed Rent Index for Fremont city, Jan 2015 to Sep 2026, from Zillow Research city-level files. Read Oct 24, 2026.
- Zillow home value and rent: Zillow Research figures for Fremont from Zillow's city home values page (data through Sep 30, 2026; sales measures through Aug 31), read Oct 24, 2026. Zillow requires clear attribution.
